summary: Adds an IMAP extension that lets a client ask the server for a short text preview of a message. Mail apps can show this snippet in the message list without downloading the whole message.

eli5.summary: Like reading the first line of a letter on the envelope, so you can decide whether to open it.

questions: how to get message previews in imap
what is the imap preview capability
how long can an imap preview be
what does the lazy modifier do in imap
why generate email previews on the server
subtitle: Lets an IMAP mail client ask the server for a short, ready-made text preview of each message.

tldr.problem: Mail apps like to show a snippet of each message in the list, but making one on the client takes several round trips and may download far more data than needed.
tldr.mechanism: A server that advertises the PREVIEW capability returns a preview string through a new FETCH data item. An optional LAZY modifier lets the server answer NIL instead of making the client wait.
tldr.outcome: Clients get consistent previews cheaply and can fill them in the background. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8970 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2020, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. IANA added the PREVIEW capability to the IMAP Capabilities registry.

sections.title: Why Servers Should Make Previews
sections.content:
Many mail clients show a small extract of the body text so a user can quickly decide whether a message is worth opening. RFC 8970 defines an extension to IMAP (the Internet Message Access Protocol, RFC 3501) so that the server generates this preview. A server announces support with the PREVIEW capability name.

The RFC gives three reasons. First, previews look the same on every client the user owns. Second, it is cheaper: a client-side approach needs a FETCH BODYSTRUCTURE first and then at least one FETCH BODY, and these cannot be pipelined because the first answer must be parsed before the second request is known. The client also cannot easily predict how much data it needs, for example when stripping tags from HTML. Third, the server can generate the preview once and cache it for the life of the message.
sections.eli5: If every phone writes its own summary of a letter, they all look different and each one has to open the whole letter. If the post office writes one summary, everybody sees the same thing and it is quick.

sections.title: The PREVIEW FETCH Item
sections.content:
To get a preview, the client adds the PREVIEW attribute to a FETCH command, for example A1 FETCH 1 (PREVIEW). The server answers with a variable-length string that people are meant to read. The client is not meant to interpret it in any way.

The server SHOULD try to return the same string each time, but a client MUST NOT assume a preview never changes. A software upgrade is one example of why it might. If the server cannot produce anything meaningful, such as for an encrypted message or an unsupported content type, it MUST return a zero-length string, and clients SHOULD NOT ask again for that message.
sections.eli5: You ask the helper, "what is this letter about?" and it gives you a short note. If it truly cannot tell, it hands you a blank note, and you should not keep asking.

sections.title: Preview Text Format and Length
sections.content:
The preview is treated as text/plain data. It MUST be encoded in UTF-8 and MUST NOT be content transfer encoded. The server SHOULD strip formatting markup and do whatever else helps to make plain text.

Length is counted in preview characters, meaning single UCS characters encoded in UTF-8, so one may take several octets. The server SHOULD limit previews to 200 preview characters and MUST NOT output more than 256. If the preview is not based on the message body (for example a message that is only an image) and the server supports the LANGUAGE extension, the descriptive text SHOULD follow the language rules for human-readable text.
sections.eli5: The note has to be plain writing, not fancy formatting, and it has to be short: about 200 letters is the goal and 256 is the most allowed.

sections.title: The LAZY Modifier
sections.content:
Writing a preview can be slow. Adding (LAZY) after PREVIEW tells the server to return the preview only if it can do so without undue delay. Otherwise it MUST return NIL. A server MUST NOT return NIL when LAZY was not used, and every server that supports PREVIEW MUST implement LAZY.

The intended client strategy is to include PREVIEW (LAZY) in the fetch that builds the mailbox listing, so the basic message list is not held up. Messages that came back NIL are then fetched without LAZY, in the background. The RFC recommends small batches, for example 50 messages per command. A client SHOULD NOT keep repeating LAZY requests in a selected mailbox, since the server need not ever answer them.
sections.eli5: "Lazy" means "only tell me if it is easy." If the helper is busy, it says "not now" and you ask again later while you are already reading your list.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives three examples. The first checks the CAPABILITY response for PREVIEW and fetches RFC822.SIZE PREVIEW for one message. The second, shown in the diagram, fetches messages 1 to 4 with ENVELOPE PREVIEW (LAZY). Message 1 returns text, message 2 returns an empty string (so no preview exists), and messages 3 and 4 return NIL, so the client then sends FETCH 3:4 (PREVIEW).

The third example combines a SEARCH RETURN (SAVE) with the SEARCHRES extension so the preview fetch can use the saved result ($) and save a round trip.
sections.eli5: The client asks for four notes. It gets one note, one blank note and two "not now" answers, so it asks again just for the last two.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Making previews costs memory, CPU and possibly storage, so the extension could be used for denial of service. To help track abusive clients, servers SHOULD log the client's authentication identity on FETCH PREVIEW operations. Servers MAY limit the resources spent on previews, which in an extreme case could mean an empty preview for a message that would otherwise have one. The RFC recommends still giving at least some text, even if of lower quality.

A preview may hold sensitive data just like the message it summarizes. If previews are stored on the server, for example as a cache, they MUST be protected with equivalent authorization and confidentiality controls as the source message.
sections.eli5: A summary can be secret too, so it must be locked up just like the letter. And the helper can say "slow down" to someone who keeps asking too much.
